si_4_title.answer: A normative modelling approach reveals age-atypical cortical thickness in a subgroup of males with autism spectrum disorder

nm2_1_modeling_methods.supporting_text: We used a local polynomial regression fitting procedure (LOESS) [34,35], where the local width or smoothing kernel of the regression was determined by the model that provided the overall smallest sum of squared errors using hyperparameter optimization across 5–100% of the full age range

nm2_2_response_variable.detail: Cortical thickness (CT); Cortical volume; Surface area; Gyrification (LGI)
nm2_2_response_variable.supporting_text: All analyses were done on CT averaged within 308 cortical regions... To show applicability of this approach we also applied the same method to other measures of neuroanatomy; gyrification, volume and surface area.

nm2_3_explanatory_variables.supporting_text: Normative modelling of age-related CT effects was done utilizing male-only data from the typically developing group (TD)... We used a local polynomial regression fitting procedure (LOESS)...
